test_title: PYST 39: SSC GD Constable 2025 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 21 Feb, 2025 - Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: Pinki, Chinki and Reema started a work and Reema left after 4 days when 46% of the work is completed and then work got completed in 9 more days. In how many days can Reema alone complete the work?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Total Work = 100%.

Combined efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki + Reema) = 46% ÷ 4 days = 11.5% per day.

Combined efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki) = (100% − 46%) ÷ 9 days = 54% ÷ 9 = 6% per day.

Reema's efficiency = 11.5% − 6% = 5.5% per day.

Time taken by Reema alone = 100% ÷ 5.5% = 1000 ÷ 55 = 200/11 = 18²/₁₁ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18²/₁₁ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Let the total work be 100 units.

⇒ Work completed by Pinki, Chinki and Reema in 4 days = 46% of 100 = 46 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 100 − 46 = 54 units.

⇒ Pinki and Chinki completed the remaining 54 units in 9 days.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki + Reema) = 46 ÷ 4 = 11.5 units/day.

⇒ Days required by them for full work = 100 ÷ 11.5 = 200/23 days.

⇒ Efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki) = 54 ÷ 9 = 6 units/day.

⇒ Days required by them for full work = 100 ÷ 6 = 50/3 days.

⇒ Efficiency of Reema = Efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki + Reema) − Efficiency of (Pinki + Chinki)

⇒ Efficiency of Reema = 11.5 − 6 = 5.5 units/day.

⇒ Time taken by Reema alone = Total Work ÷ Efficiency

⇒ Time taken = 100 ÷ 5.5 = 1000/55 = 200/11 days.

⇒ 200 ÷ 11 = 18 with a remainder of 2 = 18²/₁₁ days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18²/₁₁ days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Work and Efficiency

Total work is considered as the LCM of the days taken by individuals. Efficiency is inversely proportional to time: Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time Taken.

Persons Leaving Mid-way

When a person leaves before completing the work, calculate the work done by them during their active days. Subtract this from the total work, and the remaining work is divided by the efficiency of the remaining workers.

Percentage Based Work

When total work is given in percentages instead of days, always assume Total Work = 100% or 100 units to bypass complex fractional calculations.
